# Replication Text

This book teaches R, reproducible research, and AI-assisted empirical work through replication.

The first version starts with two chapters:

- Chapter 1, Introduction, is a placeholder for the instructor's framing.
- Chapter 2, Walker, is the first replication unit.

The Walker unit uses Walker et al. [-@walker2023anticipatory], a short paper estimating whether the anticipated repeal of *Roe v. Wade* changed the share of female applicants to selective colleges in states where abortion was banned or restricted after *Dobbs*. Students rebuild the research design, learn the R workflow, and then extend the analysis with Title IX pregnancy and parenting policy information from The Pregnant Scholar policy directory [@pregnantscholar_policy].

## What Students Practice

- Turning a published paper into a replication plan.
- Building a clean R project with raw data, scripts, outputs, and documentation.
- Estimating a fixed-effects event-study model.
- Using AI to speed up coding and source extraction while still checking the work.
- Writing about what replicates, what does not, and why.

## Background Notes

Earlier scaffold material is stored under `support/old-scaffold/`. Those files are not part of the rendered book right now, but they preserve useful notes on R workflow, data collection, AI use, and the Title IX extension.
